result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers catch every real problem in the CSS: line length, leading, tracking, justification, the backwards h1, the unspaced uppercase tag, and the invisible links. B ranks its fixes from most to least damaging and names the two that matter most, so it scores better on prioritization. A wrongly claims Georgia has no true bold italic, which counts as an invented problem; B's suggestion of tabular-nums is probably ineffective on Georgia, but that is a smaller slip. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers find all the main problems and give good corrected CSS. A explicitly ranks the fixes from most to least damaging and names the two that matter most. B says Georgia has no true bold italic, which is false because Georgia ships a Bold Italic face. B also replaces the font for prices, which goes beyond what the CSS actually shows is wrong. A's tabular-nums suggestion may have no effect in Georgia, but that is a minor slip, not a made-up problem.
